conventions.convention: Fractional integrals use Lebesgue integration on a positive finite horizon. For L1 data they are defined almost everywhere; for continuous data the integral is finite at every node, with value zero at the initial time.

The Caputo order satisfies 0 < α < 1. Its domain consists of absolutely continuous functions with separately known integrable almost-everywhere derivative; Countable Choice supplies that derivative property for the whole absolutely continuous class.

Caputo–Volterra equivalence assumes Countable Choice and Dependent Choice and an already absolutely continuous solution. Differential equality is almost everywhere; Volterra equality is everywhere. Continuous mild solutions are not asserted to be absolutely continuous.
L1 grids are finite and strictly increasing from 0 to T > 0; power grading uses r ≥ 1. The scalar coefficient λ is nonnegative, and updates run from n = 1 through N.
CQ acts on the shifted sequence V = U − u0 with V0 = 0; its forcing is F − λu0. The weights start at ω0 = 1 and obey ωj = ((j − 1 − α)/j)ω(j−1).
The CQ symbol is the holomorphic principal-branch power exp(α Log(1 − z)) on |z| < 1; real-power identities are used only after restricting to real z in (−1,1).

The uniform L1 rate assumes Countable Choice and u ∈ C2([0,T]), including one-sided endpoint derivatives. Nodal forcing uses the finite pointwise Caputo integral representative. No constant uniform as α approaches 1 is claimed.
The first-order CQ error theorem concerns only u(t) = u0 + t² with u′(0) = 0; its constant depends on α and T and is independent of N, u0, and λ ≥ 0.
Full-history counts count the terms in the displayed direct sums, including zero-valued terms. Solution-storage counts exclude input and weight storage.

load_bearing.statement: For β > 0 and g ∈ L1(0,T), Iβg(t) = Γ(β)−1 ∫0t (t−s)^(β−1)g(s) ds almost everywhere. For 0 < α < 1 and absolutely continuous u with u′ ∈ L1, DCαu = I^(1−α)u′.
For β > 0 and t > 0, ∫0t (t−s)^(β−1) ds = tβ/β.
For T > 0, a,b > 0, and g ∈ L1(0,T), Ia(Ibg) = I^(a+b)g almost everywhere and ||Iag||1 ≤ Ta||g||1/Γ(a+1). For continuous g the semigroup identity holds everywhere; Ic1(t) = tc/Γ(c+1) for c > 0.

For 0 < α < 1, λ ≥ 0, and any finite strictly increasing grid, the L1 weights are positive and nondecreasing in k; discrete comparison holds. If e0 = 0 and δTαen + λen = rn with |rn| ≤ R, then max |en| ≤ TαR/Γ(1+α). The L1 recurrence uniquely solves its discrete equation.

For 0 < α < 1, ω0 = 1 and ωj < 0 for j ≥ 1. The generating function is the principal-branch (1−z)α on |z| < 1. The partial sum pn equals Γ(n+1−α)/(Γ(1−α)Γ(n+1)) > 0, and pn ≥ (n+1)^(−α)/Γ(1−α) for n ≥ 1.
For 0 < α < 1, λ ≥ 0, T > 0, and h = T/N with N ≥ 1, CQ uniquely solves its shifted recurrence. For zero initial data and forcing gn, max |Vn| ≤ Γ(1−α)(2T)α max |gn|.
For T > 0, 0 < α < 1, A,L ≥ 0, and continuous nonnegative y satisfying y ≤ A + LIαy, one has y(t) ≤ A Σ(k≥0) Lk t^(kα)/Γ(kα+1). The series converges uniformly on [0,T]; A = 0 implies y = 0.
For T > 0, 0 < β < 1, and continuous g, Iβg is continuous, vanishes at zero, has supremum norm at most Tβ||g||∞/Γ(β+1), and satisfies |Iβg(t)−Iβg(s)| ≤ 2||g||∞|t−s|β/Γ(β+1).

For 0 < α < 1 and β = 2−α, let cm = Γ(m+β+1)/(Γ(β+1)Γ(m+1)), s1 = 1, and sn = c(n−1)+c(n−2) for n ≥ 2. Then |sn−2nβ/Γ(β+1)| ≤ Cα n^(β−1) for every n ≥ 1. These sn are the coefficients of z(1+z)(1−z)^(α−3).
Under Countable Choice, for 0 < α < 1, λ ≥ 0, a uniform grid on [0,T], and u ∈ C2([0,T]) with exact nodal forcing, max |Un−u(tn)| ≤ Cα Tα||u″||∞ h^(2−α)/Γ(1+α), where Cα = [1/(1−α)+(1+α)/2]/Γ(1−α).

seams_checked.note: Checked the citing page against the supplier page and its midpoint/Simpson definitions and error statements. The supplier gives smooth-integrand C2 midpoint and C4 Simpson bounds, without a fractional-kernel theorem.
